Let <MATH_0001> be a category.
Let <MATH_0002> be a category fibred in groupoids.
The following are equivalent:
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0003> is a category fibred in setoids, and
<STRUCT_0003> the canonical <MATH_0004>-morphism <MATH_0005>,
see (<REF_0001>), is an equivalence (of categories
over <MATH_0006>).
<STRUCT_0004>

Assume (2). The category <MATH_0001> has objects
<MATH_0002> where <MATH_0003>, say with <MATH_0004>, and
<MATH_0005> is a morphism in <MATH_0006>. Hence if
<MATH_0007> is an equivalence over <MATH_0008>
then every pair of objects <MATH_0009>, <MATH_0010> are isomorphic
in the fibre category of <MATH_0011> over <MATH_0012>.
Looking at the definition of morphisms in <MATH_0013>
we conclude that <MATH_0014>, <MATH_0015> are conjugate in the group
of automorphisms of <MATH_0016>. Hence taking <MATH_0017> we conclude
that every automorphism of <MATH_0018> is equal to the identity.
Since <MATH_0019> is fibred in groupoids this
implies that <MATH_0020> is fibred in setoids.
We omit the proof of (1) <MATH_0021> (2).
